definition: per-turn TTFT = the TTFT of the turn's own initial request: kind='turn-initial' when present, else the legacy kind='turn' row with definition_fallback=true; a kind='tool-followup' row is a request inside a turn and is never a turn's latency (version ttft-definition/1)

selector.name: analyze_stats.turn_latency_rows(rows) -> (selected_rows, meta)
callers: analyze() arm p50/p95 path (ttft_values runs over the selected rows, so n is the turn count)
analyze() quantile comparison path (compare() is handed report['arms'][arm]['ttft']['values'], i.e. the same selected values)
paired_by_turn(rows_a, rows_b) (selects both sides before indexing; reports dropped_followup_a/b and definition_fallback_a/b)
CLI analyze_stats.py --rows (prints one definition line per arm before any figure)
CLI analyze_stats.py --check-definition (definition_violations(); exit 3 on a violation)

evidence.consequence_one_sentence: Every published tools-on per-turn latency figure quoted the last follow-up of the turn, not the turn's own initial request, over a population that counted follow-up sends as turns (G8 published p95 at n=70, G9 at n=61, while each cell holds 48 turns); the p50 correction is small and its sign is not uniform (G7 +1.18 ms, G8 -4.15 ms, G9 -2.78 ms), but under one row per turn both published tools-on p95 values (397.4 ms and 429.7 ms) fall to n=48 and must be REFUSED, not restated.

G9 V6-TOOLS p95 429.696 ms [318.804, 477.058] at n=61 - same defect; per-turn n=48, p95 must be REFUSED
G8/G9/G7 p50 (and the G7 p50 198.723 ms at n=51) quoted the last follow-up for the 3/13/17 turns that made one: small, sign-consistent-with-noise moves (G7 +1.18, G8 -4.15, G9 -2.78 ms)

assumptions: No human answerer (automated tag): the definition was chosen as the operator's stated metric (p95 TTFT over a long run = time to START answering a turn) rather than asked; the rejected alternative is argued in docs/TTFT-DEFINITION.md section 2.

No rows file on disk carries kind='turn-initial', so the 'both definitions' table could not be produced from cells that have both kinds: it reports the published (all-rows) population, the per-turn selector population, and the only definition-TRUE subset available offline (turns that made one send). This is a measured limit, not a shortcut.

definition_fallback is set on every legacy cell (any selected row that is not kind='turn-initial') as the card requires, while mirrored_turns isolates the rows that are known to quote the wrong send; tools-off cells are therefore labelled but value-identical (verified against the published p50 for G1/G3/G4/G5/G6/G10).
Offline: zero inference requests; the impact generator only reads row files and LATENCY-REPORT.json.
The impact generator lives at /tmp/ttft_impact.py (this sandbox keeps /tmp ephemeral, so the byte-produced artefact - not the script - is the deliverable).
